Snapline 2.36.0

15 September 2026 · GIFs play in Snapline, a GIF can be re-cut from its recording, Convert to GIF moves into the Trim Editor, and recording and GIF cards get the still card's frame.

New

  • GIFs play in Snapline. Play on a GIF's card or tile opens it in a player of its own, with a frame scrubber and a counter that reads position over total in frames and in seconds ("119 / 239 · 11.8 / 23.9 s"), so the seconds can never be mistaken for the GIF's length. The GIF's own actions sit beside it.
  • Adjust GIF. A GIF remembers the recording it was converted from. "Adjust GIF…" reopens the Trim Editor on that recording, seeded with the GIF's crop and range, and Replace GIF writes a new GIF in its place: same History entry, same file name. The export runs beside the original and is swapped in only when it succeeds, so a cancel or a failure leaves the GIF you had untouched.
  • Convert to GIF, in one window. The GIF options no longer have a window of their own. Convert to GIF… opens the Trim Editor with a crop layer over the player, the range on the scrubber, and the presets, size, frame rate, speed, dither and loop controls under it with the live size estimate. Convert is the footer's single click; progress stays on the card's pill or the History tile as before. "Show these options each time" still turns the card's GIF button into a one-click conversion with the remembered options.
  • Recording and GIF cards wear the still card's frame. The frosted frame the still card shows on hover now surrounds recordings and GIFs too. A recording card carries Star and Reveal in Finder down the left, dismiss, Copy and Save on the right, and Play and GIF across the bottom band; GIF reads Cancel while a conversion runs. The caption reads length over size and format. A GIF card carries Play across the band and leads its caption with the loop length. Recording cards are keyboard-navigable now.
  • One editor per recording. A Trim window and a Convert or Adjust window never open side by side on the same recording; asking for the second brings the first forward. A conversion the app refuses now says why in the feedback bubble, and the options lock while an export is running.

Fixed

  • Flipping a GIF option could quit the app. Changing Dither gradients, or any option, while the size estimate was still reading the recording could take Snapline down, and Cancel mid-conversion could do the same. The reader is now stopped only by the thread that owns it.
  • Live zoom follows the cursor on display and region takes. With Highlight Clicks off, a zoom on a display or region recording landed where you pressed and never panned. It follows the pointer now, as window recordings always did.
  • Recording controls readable in Light Mode. The floating pill and its edge tab draw white on dark glass, and under Light Mode the glass went near-white over a light desktop. The panel is pinned to dark now, collapsed timer included.

Snapline 2.35.0

14 September 2026

  • Collections: Group captures by project. The History window gains a sidebar with All Captures, Starred and one row per Collection, each wearing a four-thumbnail cover, plus an overview page of cover cards. A Collection is a label, not a folder: a capture can sit in several, and the file on disk never moves. Anything in a Collection is kept — exempt from auto-delete like a starred capture — and deleting a Collection deletes no capture. Drag tiles onto a sidebar row or a cover card to add them, or use Add to Collection ▸ on a tile's menu. Inside a Collection, ⌫ and the hover ✕ mean Remove from Collection; Move to Trash stays in the menu.
  • Custom order, and a project view: Each Collection opens on a project header with its cover, a note, and a Newest | Custom order. Custom order reorders by drag and carries through Quick Look, Export (numbered names) and Combine, so a walkthrough exports in the order you arranged it.
  • File new captures as they land: Choose File New Captures Into ▸ from the menu bar and every capture — stills, scrolling captures, recordings, GIFs, imports and Combine output — joins that Collection the moment it is saved. A dot on the status icon and a chip on the Quick Access card say filing is on, with a one-click way back out. A GIF inherits its recording's Collections; a Combine result the union of its sources'.
  • Screenshots | Recordings | GIFs: A chip row above the History grid narrows any view to one medium, with a count per chip, and stays put as you move between All Captures, Starred and Collections. Starred moves into the sidebar, and the History toolbar now draws over the grid so tiles never show through its buttons.
  • Updates no longer wait for a quit that never comes: A menu-bar app is never quit, so with "Automatically download and install updates" on, Sparkle could hold a downloaded update for up to a week and then offer one the feed had already superseded. An update found by a scheduled check is now announced in the status menu — "Snapline X is available…" — and, when automatic install is on, installs itself the first time the app is quiet: no capture running, nothing being filed, no window or pin on screen. Until then the row reads "Install Snapline X and Relaunch", for whenever you would rather not wait. A recording still finalizes before the relaunch.
  • Help: The feature tour lists Collections.

Snapline 2.34.1

13 September 2026 · A fix for a crash in Settings → Shortcuts. It follows 2.34.0 on the same day, so that release's notes are repeated below.

Fixed

  • Clicking a shortcut row no longer quits the app. On some Macs, clicking Capture — or any row — in Settings → Shortcuts to record a new chord took the whole app down, and the eyedropper's value label could go the same way. The labels' typeface tripped a fault inside macOS's text engine that no app can recover from. Both now draw with the system font, the one menus print shortcuts in, with digits kept aligned, so a chord and a hex value read as they did.

New in 2.34.0, released earlier today

  • Live zoom: Press ⌥⌘Z mid-recording and the take pushes in to 2× on whatever the pointer is over, eased in over a third of a second; press it again to come back out. The framing then follows the pointer, moving only once it nears the edge of what is on screen, so nothing jitters or drifts. While you are zoomed, a yellow guide on the recording's boundary marks exactly what is being filmed, with the magnification beside it — the guide is Snapline's own chrome and never lands in the movie. Region, window and whole-display takes all zoom. The zoom button sits on the floating recording control beside Stop and Pause, and Zoom In / Zoom Out is in the menu bar as well.
  • Zoomed in the frames, so everything downstream keeps it: The zoom is composited into the recorded frames rather than applied afterwards, so a trim, a Convert to GIF and a share all carry it, with nothing to re-export. It cannot be removed from a finished recording — one more press takes it back while the take is still running. Click rings scale and stay put with the content they ring; the keystroke capsule and the camera bubble hold their size and position through a zoom.
  • ⌥⌘Z belongs to your other apps between takes: The zoom chord is held only while a recording is running and given back the moment it ends, so ⌥⌘Z stays Step Backward in Photoshop, Illustrator and After Effects the rest of the time. It is rebindable in Settings → Shortcuts like every other chord, and Snapline's own record and zoom chords are kept out of the keystroke capsule so they never flash in the movie.
  • Help: The feature tour names the live zoom and the floating recording controls, and the Help window fits a 13-inch display again on both tabs.

Show your clicks and keys in screen recordings

  • Highlight Clicks: every mouse click draws a brief expanding ring at the pointer — dual-tone, so it reads against any background. Display and region recordings.
  • Show Keystrokes: the keys you press appear in a capsule at the bottom of the movie, with shortcuts in the same ⌃⌥⇧⌘ symbols as the Shortcuts pane. Needs the Input Monitoring permission, asked once at the toggle; a recording never fails over it — refused access just means no capsule, and Snapline says so.
  • Both overlays are drawn into the recorded frames, so trims, GIF conversions, and shares keep them. The toggles live in the Record Screen bar and Settings → Recording, are remembered, and ship off. Worth knowing: Show Keystrokes records what you type — ordinary text included — into the video.

Snapline 2.16.0

Capture with Self-Timer: frame the region first, watch the countdown, and the shot fires by itself.

Capture

  • Capture with Self-Timer. Frame the region first, then a visible countdown runs — and the shot fires by itself. The delay is for staging: open the menu or tooltip you want inside the frame while the timer counts. Selection works exactly like a normal region capture (releasing the drag starts the timer — no extra confirm), and the countdown sits inside the region with the seconds, an Esc hint, and a ✕ to cancel. Nothing steals focus, so the menu you stage stays open, and the countdown never appears in the shot.
  • Pick 3, 5, or 10 seconds from the new status-menu item beside the Self-Timer setting — its top row remembers your last-used delay for a one-click repeat — or bind a shortcut in Settings → Shortcuts (it ships unbound). A canceled timer saves nothing and says so.
  • The invisible delay is gone. If you keep a sticky Self-Timer default set, region and main-display captures now show this same live countdown instead of silently stalling before the crosshair — same delay, visible and cancellable.

Snapline 2.15.0

History learns starred captures. The relaunch now waits for the old copy to actually exit.

History

  • History learns starred captures. Star anything worth keeping and it survives the retention sweep unconditionally — it never expires, and a starred card asks before a manual delete goes through. Star from the card's hover control or its Star/Unstar menu item; a starred capture wears a badge at rest. The History toolbar gains a Starred filter that combines with search.

Robustness

  • Fixed: Snapline could quit itself and not come back after you answered the Screen Recording prompt. The relaunch waited a fixed half-second before reopening, which could fire while the old copy was still shutting down — so nothing came back, and no crash report explained it. The relaunch now waits for the old copy to actually exit, and when it can't reopen safely it stays running and tells you instead of vanishing. The prompt for one permission no longer triggers a relaunch offer for another.
  • Also fixed: the camera bubble no longer scans for cameras on the main thread, which could stall the Record Screen bar (and probe for nearby iPhones) each time it opened; its window now closes cleanly instead of racing an in-flight animation; and the bubble's style controls no longer risk a crash from a settings change or a removed gradient stop.
